mechanism_narrative: The INSR-IL6ST forced-proximity novokine (flexible_GS4 linker, ~20 Å) brings an RTK (INSR, Tyr kinase) into close apposition with a cytokine receptor (IL6ST/gp130, JAK-associated). Under forced co-clustering, INSR's kinase domain transphosphorylates IL6ST's intracellular tyrosines, creating docking sites for SHC1, GRB2, and PIK3R1 that are not efficiently engaged by IL6ST alone (which signals primarily through JAK-STAT). Simultaneously, IL6ST-associated JAK1/2 transphosphorylate INSR's juxtamembrane tyrosines, enhancing IRS1/2 and STAT3 recruitment beyond what INSR alone achieves. The short GS4 linker (~20 Å) sterically excludes large adaptors like PLCG1 (which requires ~40+ Å spacing for productive docking), biasing output toward PI3K-AKT-mTOR and RAS-MAPK-ERK pathways while suppressing PLCγ-Ca²⁺ and atypical PKC signaling. This biased signaling profile upregulates muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN) and downregulates aged-muscle IEGs and inflammatory markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP), consistent with a rejuvenating transcriptional shift.
